transcript:
User: Before anything — what does this cost? I'm not paying some monthly subscription ripoff.
Agent: Totally hear you—I wouldn’t either if it didn’t pay for itself. Before I throw out numbers, what kind of business are you (HVAC, appliance repair/handyman, garage door/locksmith, or something else)?
User: I'm a med spa owner. Let's cut to the chase—how much is this going to cost me?
Agent: Got it. We’re not a “random subscription” — pricing depends on how many locations/lines you have and how much call volume you want us to handle, but most med spas land around **$1,200–$2,800/month** because it’s built to recover missed consult bookings and after-hours inquiries.  

How many locations and main phone lines are you running?
User: $1,200–$2,800? That's steep. I just have one location. What's the catch? You sure it's worth it?
Agent: Makes sense—if it’s one location, the “catch” is really just whether you’re currently missing enough consults during treatments/after-hours for it to pay back. Roughly, if we help you recover even **2–4 consults a month** that convert, it usually covers that range for a med spa.  

About how many calls or consult inquiries do you think you miss in a typical week because you’re with clients or it’s after hours?
User: I miss about 12 calls a week. But what's the cost if the service doesn't work?
Agent: Got it—12 a week is a lot of money sitting on the table for a med spa. When you say “doesn’t work,” do you mean it’s not booking consults, or that the calls feel off-brand and you don’t want it answering?
User: I mean paying for a service that doesn't convert those missed calls into actual bookings. What's the price?
Agent: Yeah, totally fair. For a **single-location med spa**, you’re typically looking at **$1,200–$2,800/month**, and the exact spot in that range depends mostly on **call volume and whether you want it booking directly into your calendar** versus just capturing and handing off warm leads.

To make sure I’m giving you the right number: do you want it to **book appointments/consults automatically**, or just **capture the caller info and reason** for your team to confirm?
User: $1,200–$2,800? Steep for one location. My cousin paid less and got nothing. Why so high?
Agent: I hear you—if your cousin paid and it didn’t turn into booked consults, that would sour anyone. Ours is higher because it’s built to actually **book** (not just “answer”), handle med-spa questions like Botox/filler/laser, and capture after-hours inquiries so you’re not losing those 12 missed calls a week.  

When those 12 missed calls happen, are they mostly **during treatments**, or **after hours/weekends**?
User: Mostly during treatments. But again, what's this going to cost me monthly? Need a number.
Agent: Got it—mostly during treatments. For a one-location med spa, it’s typically **$1,200–$2,800/month**, and the exact number comes down to your call volume and whether you want it **booking consults** or just **capturing and handing off**.  

Do you want it to actually **book appointments/consults** while you’re in treatment, or just take details for your front desk to call back?
User: $1,200–$2,800? My cousin paid less and got nothing. Why is yours worth more?
Agent: Makes sense—there are a lot of “answers calls” tools that don’t actually turn missed med spa inquiries into booked consults.

Dialux is priced higher because it’s set up to (1) handle the real med spa questions (Botox units, filler syringes, laser packages), (2) capture intent and follow up immediately instead of just taking a message, and (3) book consults while you’re in treatment so those 12 missed calls don’t drift to the next clinic.

What happens today when you miss a call during a treatment—do they go to voicemail, text, or a front-desk callback list?
User: They usually go to voicemail or a callback list. But seriously, what's the exact cost for this service?
Agent: Got it—voicemail plus a callback list. I can’t give an exact monthly number on this call because it’s set by your call volume and whether you want it booking into your calendar, but for one-location med spas it typically lands **between $1,200 and $2,800/month**.  

Has anyone ever shown you the quick math on what those **12 missed calls a week** are likely costing you?
User: $1,200–$2,800? That's steep for one location. What's the catch? You sure it's worth it?
Agent: No catch—if it doesn’t recover booked consults, it’s not worth it, and I wouldn’t push it on you. Mind if I do a 30‑second calculation using your 12 missed calls a week to see what “worth it” would look like in your numbers?
User: Fine, but I'm skeptical. Show me the numbers and let's see if it's worth my time.
Agent: Got it. Of those **12** missed calls a week, what percentage do you think would actually book a consult/treatment if you picked up—**30%**, **50%**, or **70%**?
User: I'd say about 55% would book, but again, what's this service going to cost me exactly?
Agent: Got it—55%. And what’s your average ticket when someone does book (ballpark): **$400**, **$650**, or **$850**?
User: Average appointment is $320. But enough with the questions—what's the price for this service?
Agent: Totally—here’s the math using your numbers: **12 missed calls/week × 55% booking × $320** is about **$2112 extra a week**… and that’s roughly **$9100/mo**.  

Knowing that, does **$1,200–$2,800/month** feel more like “steep,” or more like “if it reliably books, it’s worth it”?
User: If it really books, it might be worth it. Let's do the free demo call to evaluate.
Agent: Perfect—Jay’s the one who runs that demo and can show exactly how it would book missed calls for your med spa. What’s your first name?
User: My name's Priya. Let's see if this demo can actually show me the value without any hidden costs.
Agent: Got it, Priya—totally fair, Jay can walk through pricing and what’s included so there are no surprises. What’s your last name?
User: My last name is Nair. Let's see if your demo can prove it's worth the cost.
Agent: Makes sense, Priya. What’s the name of your medical spa?
User: It's Nair Med Spa in Brooklyn, NY. Let's see if your demo can prove it's worth the cost.
Agent: Got it—Nair Med Spa. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in Eastern Time, Brooklyn, NY. Now, let's see if this demo truly justifies the cost.
Agent: Got it—Eastern time. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the SMS confirmation?
User: Yes, the number I'm calling from works. Send me the SMS confirmation for the demo.
Agent: One moment while I check availability. Would you prefer later today or tomorrow for the demo?
User: Tomorrow works best. Please confirm the exact time and send a reminder.
Agent: Got it—tomorrow. I can get you in as soon as **6:30 PM** or **7:15 PM** Eastern time; which works?
User: Let's do 7:15 PM Eastern time. Send me a confirmation text, please.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Priya — you’re booked for **tomorrow at 7:15 PM Eastern**. You’ll receive an **SMS text** with the confirmation details, and you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Just make sure it's confirmed and remind me with a text.
Agent: It’s confirmed, Priya—you’ll get an SMS text with all the details, and you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to. Really glad you called—Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day. Bye!
